title: Ang 475–484: Kabir in Asa

segments.voice: A week in the middle of Asa. Sweet will. The lament. The letters. Songs of union. The dawn ballad. And yesterday, the thread: compassion for cotton, worn on the inside.
screen: `SWEET WILL · THE LAMENT · THE LETTERS.` → `SONGS OF UNION · THE DAWN BALLAD.` → `THE THREAD.`

segments.voice: Every hoodie, every bedsheet, every pair of jeans started on a loom: long threads pulled tight, and one thread crossing them, over and under, over and under. Kabir knew looms. Tradition says he was a weaver, and in his Asa hymns the trade shows through. Near the end of them, on ang 484, he says, in paraphrase: nobody knows the weaver's secret; he stretched the whole world out as his warp.
screen: `OVER AND UNDER, OVER AND UNDER.` → `KABIR KNEW LOOMS.` → `THE WHOLE WORLD AS A WARP.`

segments.voice: Kabir's hymns in Raag Asa run from ang 475 to 484, a weaver singing in the raga we've walked for two weeks. In that hymn on ang 484 he turns his own trade into a picture of the One: earth and sky as the loom, the whole world stretched tight like the long threads before the weaving starts. The warp is the part you set up first, and everything else is woven across it. It's yesterday's thread, made enormous. Guru Nanak asked for a thread of compassion for one soul. Kabir sees a weaver whose threads hold everything. Put the week together, and Asa has been a loom of its own: a will that tastes sweet; a lament that counts each braid; letters that ask for an account; songs where every listener is the bride; a dawn ballad full of wonder; a thread worn on the inside. Different voices, a Guru's and a weaver's, one cloth.
screen: `KABIR, THE WEAVER, IN ASA.` · `THE WORLD STRETCHED AS A WARP.` · `YESTERDAY'S THREAD, MADE HUGE.` · `ONE WEEK, ONE CLOTH.` · then, large: `KABIR IN ASA.`

segments.voice: Read one hymn on ang 476 first if you can. Then find a piece of woven cloth near you, a sleeve, a scarf, a dish towel, and look closely: threads running one way, threads crossing them. Rest your eyes on the weave for the sit, and let each crossing stand for one thing this week held together.
Ang 475. The page where Kabir's hymns in Raag Asa begin.
Your line: Kabir in Asa, a weaver who sees the whole world on one loom. Two weeks, woven.
